learning_outcomes.text: Evaluate and thermodynamically size energy conversion systems, particularly those commonly used in industrial plants.

Recognize and classify the main and most common energy systems, describe the operating principles of their various components, and carry out performance assessments of the plants based on energy balances, taking into account the relevant characteristics of the fluid machineries used.
Identify algorithmic approaches and use databases to achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes.
Apply the principles of thermodynamics to energy systems described by the main thermodynamic cycles.
Select and apply appropriate analytical and modelling methods for thermal power plants and energy conversion systems.
Assess the energy and environmental performance of conversion plants.
Demonstrate independent judgment in the preparation and selection of solution methods for the thermodynamic analysis of specific energy systems through written tests.
Present, independently, a specific topic covered during the lectures during the oral examination, demonstrating autonomous argumentation.
Demonstrate communication skills through graphical and tabular representation of thermodynamic cycles, systems and results in intermediate and preliminary written tests.
Communicate specific issues relating to energy systems clearly and rigorously, highlighting the criteria for analysis during the oral examination.
Develop models of energy conversion systems independently.
Gather further bibliographic information and develop the ability to solve problems and undertake simple projects.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to renewable Energy Systems and ORC
Energy system modeling systems using a modular object-oriented approach
Application to conventional and innovative systems
teaching_methods: Group practice on assigned projects with periodic revisions
assessment_rules: Students can take 3 intermediate tests. Passing these tests grants direct access to the oral test and final vote. If intermediate tests are not taken or passed, a student must pass a written test (similar to intermediate tests) and an oral test. A minimum sufficient knowledge of mathematical and physical modeling of energy systems, and of the energy components and systems described in the course, is required to pass.
